compiled:
📰 General

UK Government Under Pressure to Limit Energy Company Profits Amidst Crisis •

Calls are mounting for the UK government to implement a temporary cap on energy company profits following the escalating conflict in the Middle East. Richard Walker, the recently appointed Iceland boss, argues that households are particularly vulnerable to another significant price surge. The conflict is driving up global energy costs, exacerbating an already challenging situation for consumers. Experts predict continued volatility in the energy market, necessitating potential government intervention to protect vulnerable populations.

🌍 World

EU Expresses Concern as Hungary Investigates Alleged Russian Wiretapping of Minister •

The European Union has reacted with concern following reports of a potential leak of information from Hungarian Foreign Minister Peter Szijjarto to Russia. Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orban announced an investigation into the alleged “wiretapping,” claiming it constitutes a serious attack on the country. Szijjarto has not yet commented publicly on the allegations, and the investigation’s scope and potential findings remain unclear. The incident raises significant questions about Hungary’s intelligence cooperation and its relationship with Russia.

🦅 US

Supreme Court Signals Potential Restrictions on Mail-In Ballots Ahead of Midterms •

The U.S. Supreme Court indicated a potential shift in election rules, suggesting mail-in ballots arriving after election day could be excluded from counting. This stance stems from a case, Watson v. Jackson, concerning Arkansas law which prohibits mail-in ballots received after the election. The justices are evaluating the legality of such a restriction, potentially impacting voting procedures in over a dozen states during the upcoming midterm elections. The court’s decision could significantly alter the mechanics of mail-in voting across the nation.

💰 Business

Dow Jumps on Trump’s Iran Concerns, Pharma Stock Gains Ground Today •

The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose significantly today, driven largely by a warning from former President Trump regarding Iran’s nuclear program. Investors reacted positively to the geopolitical developments, contributing to a broad market rally. Additionally, a major pharmaceutical company announced its entry into a new market, boosting its stock price. The overall market performance reflects a combination of economic and geopolitical factors.

💻 Technology

Finishing Video Games Linked to Post-Game Depression, New Study Reveals •

A recent study conducted by SWPS University and the Stefan Batory Institute has investigated the psychological effects of completing video games. Researchers found a measurable phenomenon of post-game depression, characterized by feelings of emptiness and emotional exhaustion. The study suggests that the intense engagement and emotional investment in a game can lead to a significant psychological impact upon its conclusion. Participants reported experiencing reflective and draining feelings after completing a game.

🎭 Entertainment

Richard Gadd’s ‘Half Man’ Premiere Date Announced by HBO & BBC •

Richard Gadd’s new comedy series, “Half Man,” is set to premiere on April 23rd through HBO and April 24th via the BBC. The project follows Gadd’s experiences after a disastrous dating app encounter. “Half Man” marks Gadd’s first television project since the success of “Baby Reindeer,” which garnered significant critical acclaim. HBO and the BBC have released artwork to coincide with the announcement of the premiere dates.

🏅 Sports

Seven Unbeaten NCAA Champions Vie for 2026 Dan Hodge Trophy Honors •

The 2026 ASICS Race for the Dan Hodge Trophy fan vote is now open, featuring seven of the ten NCAA Division I wrestling champions from the 2026 Championships. These seven undefeated wrestlers – [list of seven wrestlers, if available from the article] – are competing for the prestigious award. The fan vote, conducted through the Win Magazine website, will determine the winner of the Dan Hodge Trophy. The 2026 NCAA DI Wrestling Championships took place in Cleveland on March 21st.

🔬 Science

NASA Announces Public Event to Detail Trump Administration’s Space Plans •

NASA will hold a public event on Tuesday, March 24th, at 9 a.m. EDT at the Mary W. Jackson NASA Headquarters. The event will focus on outlining the agency’s strategy for implementing President Donald J. Trump’s National Space Council directives. Attendees will hear details regarding NASA’s approach to achieving the goals outlined in the council’s strategic plan. The event is open to the public and will be streamed online.

🩺 Health

Brain’s Overdrive Response in Aging Increases Fall Risk, Study Finds •

Research indicates that the brain’s compensatory mechanisms in older adults, specifically the “overdrive” response to maintain balance, are linked to an increased risk of falls. The study observed that older individuals utilize a more prolonged and complex neural response compared to younger adults when challenged with balance disturbances. This extended neural activity, while effective in maintaining stability, appears to contribute to a greater vulnerability to falls. Scientists believe this heightened brain activity may be a consequence of the brain’s attempt to counteract age-related changes in balance control.
